# $crav1-review-pr

lane: cross-cutting | group: Commit and pull request | starter: no | stage: stable | since: 1.6.0 | prompts: 2
purpose: Read one named open pull request and report whether it can ship.
use_when: This turn names an open pull request
reads: Reads one named open pull request, its diff, the spec, the body, and the required linter. When the slug has `plan.md`, also reads the plan and `verify.md`. When the slug has no `plan.md` or `tasks.md`, reads the pipeline's recorded test results instead and does not treat a missing `verify.md` as a finding.
writes: Writes the PR note in `docs/notes/YYYY-MM/` with its `## PR record` (a Point per finding, follow-up and question) and regenerates the notes indexes, updating the same note on a re-review, with the comment as drafted and as posted in its history. After the user's yes, posts one comment and the matching vote.
leaves alone: Leaves code, the spec, the plan, and the merge alone. Never resolves a thread without a yes.
limits: spark, specify, verify, `$crav1-open-pr`, and `$crav1-merge-pr` do not run it. An outside pull request names `$crav1-refresh-system-notes` after merge and does not run it.
flow:
- a bare number (`82`, `pr82`, `PR 82`) is resolved from the kit's records first (`pr_common.py resolve`: build-progress files, the merge list, PR notes, `docs/system/repos.md`).
- It names only the CLI of the resolved host and ends with Run next, never a `Next:` line.
- The merge order comes from the ready check's merge list and `build-progress/`, not the description, or it says the kit has none recorded.
- `scripts/ado_threads.py list`, `compare --draft <file>` and `post --file <file> --yes` read and post Azure DevOps threads.
- It reads `az -o json` from stdout as bytes and decodes UTF-8, then UTF-8 with a BOM, then cp1252, so a Windows code page no longer breaks the JSON.
- A post is always a new top-level thread.
- `comment-as-posted.md` is read only when the PR note's draft has no `## Comment as posted` section.
- After the post offer the reply ends with Run next (`$crav1-finalize-commit`, then `git push`) while the PR note is uncommitted, and the Uncommitted line shows in chat.
- the fetch card for an older copy on disk follows the card wording rule in `docs/reference/question-cards.md`: one sentence names the older copy, then `Fetch the pull request's two branches before the review?`.
- the shared pull-request steps are `crav1-docs/reference/pr-common.md` and `scripts/pr_common.py`.
- Ship or not moved word for word to `references/ship.md`, and the one-line pointers are one list, Which file, when.
- When an open pull request is named, **`$crav1-review-pr`** reads the diff and says whether it can ship.
- A pull request with a plan keeps the plan and `verify.md` checks.
- A pull request with no `plan.md` or `tasks.md` for its slug was built outside the kit.
- It does not report a missing `verify.md`.
- It ends by naming `$crav1-refresh-system-notes` after the merge and does not run it.
- Follow-ups, including choices the description calls deliberate, are not posted and not in that comment; they are saved in the PR note's shared PR record (one `follow-up` Point each, with its file and line, 1.97.0), which a re-review updates and `$crav1-ado-sync` reads as open items.
- It never resolves a thread without your yes.
- `$crav1-open-pr` may name it and does not run it.
- `$crav1-merge-pr` does not run it.
- When the slug has `plan.md`, spec, plan, `verify.md`, the body, and a required green linter must hold before it says ship.
- When the slug has no `plan.md` or `tasks.md`, that is an info note.
- It does not report a missing `verify.md`.
- It names `$crav1-refresh-system-notes` after that pull request merges and does not run it.
- finds the spec the same way as `$crav1-open-pr`, including a spec that lists the head branch.
- the comment follows `references/comment-layout.md`: no verdict line, one short plain opening, Blockers, Bugs, Tests to add with this PR, and A question, each point starting with the host link to its file and line on the source branch and then an indented paragraph, at most one fix per point, no follow-ups, no table, no closing.
- It posts one comment, no inline threads, and votes (never Reject) only after your yes.
- Advice about merge order says to merge the base into the branch, never to rebase.
- Post it adds "I'll post it myself"; choice words `comment-posted`, `newest-comment` and `skip-comment-record`.
- Findings, follow-ups and questions go into the PR note's shared `## PR record` (`crav1-add-to-spec` `references/pr-record.md`) as Point lines, drafted points you cut get `not posted <date>`, and the comment as drafted and as posted go into the PR note's history.
- An old follow-ups note is still read; run `$crav1-add-to-spec migrate-formats` to move it.
- Thread reads follow `references/pr-threads.md` (there is no `az repos pr thread list`).
- For where every thread stands, run `$crav1-pr-status`.
- a format A description from `$crav1-open-pr` is compared with the diff bullet by bullet (each Changes bullet against the lines it links, each change against a bullet), and a choice a bullet's why calls deliberate, or that Not in this PR names as left out, is not raised as a fault unless the repo says otherwise.
- `ado_threads.py` reads the organization, project and repository from the code repo's git remote (`--code-repo`, default the current folder), so `post` no longer returns 404 without `--org`, `--project` and `--repo`; those flags still override.

## Choice words
- question: Review a branch (optional, 1.80.0)
  - `branch`: review a branch with no pull request: local diff from its base, same checks, PR-only parts skipped, verdict in chat
- question: PR branches on disk older than the pull request
  - `fetch-pr-branches`: fetch only the PR's two branches
  - `use-disk`: review the copies on disk
  - `stop-pr-review`: stop
- question: The comment as posted
  - `comment-posted`: only record the posted comment, no review
  - `newest-comment`: several candidates: take the newest match by you
  - `skip-comment-record`: do not record; the review goes on
called_by: Called by the user.
runs by itself: Calls no skill.
you run next: $crav1-merge-pr; $crav1-tighten-spec; $crav1-plan-from-spec; $crav1-build-tasks; $crav1-finalize-commit; $crav1-pr-status; $crav1-refresh-system-notes after an outside pull request merges
first: `$crav1-review-pr https://github.com/<owner>/<repo>/pull/<n> Read the diff. Do not edit. Do not run the tests. Do not merge.`
walkthrough: from-review-pr.md
human: https://github.com/Crav1on/crav1-spec-kit/blob/v1.209.0/docs/reference/skills/crav1-review-pr.md
